senses.gloss:
अर्ब् cl. 1. P. अर्बति (perf. आनर्ब, L.) to go, L.;
to hurt, L.
अर्बुक m. pl. N. of a people, MBh. ii, 1119.
अ॑र्बुद m. Ved. a serpent-like demon (conquered by Indra, a descendant of Kadrū therefore called Kādraveya, ŚBr.; AitBr.; said to be the author of RV. x, 94; RAnukr.), RV. &c.
अर्बुद॑ (अ॑स्), m. id., RV. i, 51, 6 and x, 67, 12
अ॑र्बुद (अम्), n. N. of the above-named hymn, RV. x, 94; ĀśvŚr.
अ॑र्बुद (अस्, अम्), m. n. a long round mass (said especially of the shape of the foetus in the second half of the first month [Nir. xiv, 6] or in the second month [Yājñ. iii, 75 and 89])
a swelling, tumour, polypus, Suśr. &c.
अर्बुद the cartilage of a rib, Viṣṇ.
(अ॑र्बुद), n. (also m., L.) ten millions, VS. xvii, 2, &c. (or 100 millions, See महार्बुद)
(अस्), (अस्), m. N. of a mountain in the west of India (commonly called Abū, a place of pilgrimage of the Jainas, and celebrated for its Jaina temples)
(आस्), (आस्), m. pl. N. of a people, VarBṛS.; BhP. &c.
अर्बुद (with Buddhists) N. of one of the 8 cold hells, Dharmas. 122
अर्बुद—धा ind. millionfold, JaimUp.
अर्बुद—पर्वत m. the mountain Arbuda.
अर्बुद—माहात्म्य n. N. of a ch. of the SkandaP.
अर्बुद—शिखर m. id., Hit.
अर्बुदाकार m. ‘shaped like a tumour’, the plant Cordia Myxa, L.
अर्बुदारण्य n. N. of a forest, NarasP.
अर्बु—˚दोदासर्पिणी f. ‘creeping near of Arbuda’, N. of a partic. sacrificial path, AitBr.
अ॑र्बुदि m. a serpent like demon (probably = अ॑र्बुद and अर्बुद॑ m. above, but called इ॑न्द्रमेधिन्, q.v.), AV. xi, 9 and 10 (in almost every verse) (cf. न्य्-अ॑र्बुदि.)
आर्बुदि m. (fr. अर्बुद), N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi.
अर्बुदिन् mfn. afflicted with a swelling or tumour, Suśr.
अर्बुध m. = अ॑र्बुद m. above, Kāṭh.; Anukr.
